2. The present writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs :-
(a) for quashing of order dated 28.06.2023 (Annexure-4) passed by Additional Collector-cum- Arbitrator (respondent no. 4) whereby and whereunder the respondent no. 4 has not considered the claim of the petitioner for payment of adequate/ fair compensation amount with regard to acquisition of her land for construction of NH-75 (SEC-V) on the basis of market value in terms of Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and awarded less/ meager amount of compensation than the market value,
Rajpati Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102616703/
1 (b) for issuance of an appropriate writ(s), order(s), direction(s) or a writ in the nature of mandamus commanding upon the respondents to pay the fair/ adequate compensation to the petitioner with regard to acquisition of her land for construction of National Highway-75 (SEC-V), when other land loosers namely Rajendra Pratap Dev & others whose land (agricultural/rural) situated at Village/
Mouza-- Narkhoria Kala (adjacent/ near village) was also acquired for the same purpose has received highest rate i.e. Rs.2,76,080/- (Annexure- 6) for per decimal which is highest rate in comparison to another land looser including the petitioner.
3. After some arguments, learned counsel for the petitioner seeks permission with withdraw the present writ petition with a liberty to work out his remedy in accordance with law.
4.
